q-330499.name: Question 1
q-330499.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,3,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨4,0,1⟩.$
q-330499.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-1,3,2⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨4,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =⟨-1,3,2⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =-2 \\ 4x+z & =-2 \\ 4x+z+2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−1,3,2) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨4,0,1⟩.

a
4x+z+2=0
b
4x−y+z+2=0
c
4x+y+z+2=0
d
4x+z−2=0
e
x+4y+z+2=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−1,3,2⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨4,0,1⟩.

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨4,0,1⟩=⟨−1,3,2⟩⋅⟨4,0,1⟩r⋅⟨4,0,1⟩=−2

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨4,0,1⟩=−24x+z=−24x+z+2=0.

q-127964.name: Question 2
q-127964.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(5,2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=3i-j+2k.$
q-127964.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨5,2,-1⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨3,-1,2⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =⟨5,2,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =11 \\ 3x-y+2z & =11 \\ 3x-y+2z-11 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-70815.name: Question 3
q-70815.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(0,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=2+2t \\ y=5t \\ z=1-t\end{aligned}.$
q-70815.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,3⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨2,5,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨2,5,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ & =⟨0,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$

q-70818.html:
Question 6
?

Given the Cartesian equation 2x+y−2z−4=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,1,−2⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,0,−2⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨1,0,−1⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,−2,−4⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨2,1,−2⟩=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of Π is n=⟨2,1,−2⟩.

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of Π for z: 2x+y−2z−4=0−2z=−2x−y+4z=x+12y−2. If we put, say, x=0 and y=0, we get z=−2. Hence, the point P(0,0,−2) lies on Π. Note that the position vector of P is p=⟨0,0,−2⟩.

Finally, we obtain (r−p)⋅n=0(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,1,−2⟩=0.

q-128410.name: Question 7
q-128410.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,1)$, $P(3,-1,2)$ and $Q(4,2,0).$
q-128410.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,1⟩,\,p=⟨3,-1,2⟩,$ and $q=⟨4,2,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-1,2⟩-⟨1,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨4,2,0⟩-⟨1,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+5j+5k \\  & =⟨-5,5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =⟨3,-1,2⟩\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =-10 \\ -5x+5y+5z & =-10 \\ -5x+5y+5z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}

d

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[211]×[34−1]=ijk21134−1=−5i+5j+5k=⟨−5,5,5⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−5,5,5⟩=⟨3,−1,2⟩⋅⟨−5,5,5⟩r⋅⟨−5,5,5⟩=−10

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

q-33912.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨5,2,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,3,3⟩.$
q-33912.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =3i-15j+15k \\  & =⟨3,-15,15⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =48\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =48 \\ 3x-15y+15z & =48 \\ 3x-15y+15z-48 & =0 \\ x-5y+5z-16 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
